items.title: Addressing random spatial translations in measured microphone directional responses by maximizing finite order energy
items.abstract: Directional responses measured on real-world devices are disturbed by unknown translations in space, which add uncertainty to spatial signal processing methods that use such data. In this paper we propose the concept of finite order centroid, which is the translation that maximizes directional response energy in finite order spatial harmonics. The centroid is calculated from the measured response as a second translation, to the effect that it cancels any random perturbation to the first. This leads to a calibrated directional response that is free from said positioning uncertainty, and has spatio-acoustical guarantees useful for downstream processing. We use several simple tasks to show the use of finite order centroids in spatial signal processing.

items.title: Blind Room Impulse Response Identification via Reverberant Speech Spectrum Reconstruction
items.authors: Pengyu Wang(Zhejiang University; Westlake University); Xiaofei Li(Westlake University; Westlake Institute for Advanced Study)
items.abstract: This paper proposes Rec-RIR for blind room impulse response (RIR) identification. Based on the convolutive transfer function (CTF) approximation, we propose a multi-task deep neural network, which sequentially removes noise and reverberation from speech recording, and estimates the CTF filter by reverberant speech spectrum reconstruction. Subsequently, a pseudo intrusive measurement process is employed to convert the CTF filter into RIR by simulating a common intrusive RIR measurement procedure. Experimental results demonstrate that Rec-RIR achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance in blind RIR identification.

items.title: Sensitivity Analysis of Generative Spatial Audio Metrics : A Study on Responsiveness, Smoothness, and Symmetry
items.authors: Purnima Kamath(New York University); Adrian Roman(New York University); Koichi Saito(Sony AI); Yuki Mitsufuji(Sony AI; Sony Group Corporation; New York University); Juan Bello(New York University)
items.abstract: Evaluating generative spatial audio for First-Order Ambisonics (FOA) remains challenging due to a limited understanding of how metrics respond to changes in spatial parameters such as azimuth and elevation. We propose a framework to analyze metric sensitivity along continuous spatial trajectories, drawing on principles of sensitivity analysis in parametric sound synthesis. Using controlled FOA scenes with increasing scene complexity, we define three desiderata for metric behavior: Responsiveness, Smoothness, and Symmetry. We assess standard distribution-based and sample-based metrics, including Fréchet Audio Distance (FAD), intensity vectors, and acoustic maps. Our findings show that FAD using localization-specific embeddings and acoustic maps yield high Responsiveness and robust Smoothness and Symmetry across conditions, while intensity vectors degrade with increasing scene complexity. This is the first step towards investigating the sensitivity of metrics for generative spatial audio.

items.title: FoleyImmersive: Decoupling What and Where for Video-to-First-Order Ambisonics
items.authors: Liming Liang(Peking University); Lingfeng Yang(South China University of Technology); Luo Chen(Peking University); Chenxing Li(Tencent AI Lab); Yuexian Zou(Peking University)
items.abstract: We study immersive video-to-audio (V2A) by generating first-order ambisonics (FOA) from silent field-of-view (FoV) videos. Challenges include sparse semantics in video-FOA corpora and content-geometry entanglement: end-to-end models blur "what" and "where", while two-stage pipelines trade semantic fidelity for spatial coherence. We present FoleyImmersive and a semantics-augmented dataset, YT-AmbiSem, which augments YT-Ambigen with structured descriptions from Qwen2.5-VL-7B. Stage 1 (WHAT) uses a semantics-first diffusion model with multi-rate cross-frame attention and probabilistic time modulation to generate mono W. Stage 2 (WHERE) spatializes W to XYZ via a complex-STFT U-Net conditioned on per-frame visuals and camera direction; a lightweight directional residual mixer applies view-dependent bottleneck gating to stabilize localization with minimal content drift. We achieve state-of-the-art semantic and spatial metrics. Demo and dataset are available.

items.title: Learning Self-Supervised Spatial Representations via Soft Acoustic Contrastive Alignment
items.authors: Yotam Silverman(Tel Aviv University); Bracha Laufer-Goldshtein(Tel Aviv University)
items.abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for improving downstream performance when annotated data is limited. However, most existing audio SSL methods process single-channel inputs and focus on learning spectral representations, which are often insufficient for spatially sensitive tasks like direction-of-arrival or reverberation estimation. In this work, we propose a self-supervised framework for binaural audio that integrates spatial priors directly into the pre-training objective. We introduce the Soft Acoustic Contrastive (SAC) loss, a geometric objective that structures the latent space by aligning embeddings based on shared acoustic properties, such as directionality and diffuseness, without requiring ground-truth labels. Experimental results demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms baselines across five downstream spatial parameter estimation tasks.

items.title: Geometrically Constrained Decentralized Independent Vector Analysis for Distributed Microphone Arrays
items.authors: Changda Chen(Waseda University; Nanjing University); Yichen Yang(Northwestern Polytechnical University); Wei Liu(Waseda University; Wuhan University); Bing Zhu(Northwestern Polytechnical University); Gongping Huang(Wuhan University); Shoji Makino(Waseda University); Shuai Wang(Nanjing University)
items.abstract: This paper proposes a geometrically constrained decentral-ized independent vector analysis (GC-Dec-IVA) method for distributed microphone arrays. Recently proposed Dec-IVA method enables source separation by exchanging only power-related statistics to exploit cross-array information. However, this initial attempt often provides negligible improvement over applying IVA locally at each array, mainly due to the potential permutation inconsistency among arrays and the strong cross-array dependency implied by its source model. To address these limitations, we incorporate direction-of-arrival (DOA) information to derive GC-Dec-IVA, which mitigates permutation mismatch across arrays and enhances source alignment. Furthermore, a new source model is introduced to weaken cross-array dependency, improving robustness against permutation inconsistency in noisy environments. Experiments show the proposed method improves both the separation performance and cross-array permutation consistency.

items.title: Optimal Source Placement for TDoA-based Geometry Calibration of Distributed Microphone Arrays
items.authors: Xu Wang(Inner Mongolia University); Qintuya Si(Inner Mongolia University); Qingyin Zhao(Inner Mongolia University); De Hu(Inner Mongolia University)
items.abstract: Distributed microphone arrays (DMAs) are widely used in various audio/speech processing applications. As these applications require the geometric structure of the DMA as a priori knowledge, geometry calibration of DMAs is indispensable. However, most existing methods use randomly placed calibration sources, which may lead to a relatively higher Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB). In this paper, we use a mobile robot to act as the multiple calibration sources, and optimize its positions to expect an improved self-localization accuracy. Specifically, we derive the CRLB using time-difference-of-arrival measurements with time offsets. Then, the optimal robot's positions are obtained by minimizing the CRLB while constraining the robot positions within a restricted room. Additionally, we also present a multi-stage solution for scenarios with limited computational resources or demanding runtime requirements. Numerical experiments validate the effectiveness of the proposed placement methods.

items.title: G2C-NET: A Grid-to-Continuous Neural Network for Sound Source Localization in Distributed Microphone Arrays
items.authors: Zhiyuan Yue(Inner Mongolia University); De Hu(Inner Mongolia University)
items.abstract: Grid-based sound source localization (SSL) has gained increasing attention in distributed microphone arrays as it reformulates the inherently nonconvex regression problem into a tractable classification task. However, the trade-off between grid resolution and computational complexity poses a fundamental challenge. To this end, we propose G2C-NET, a grid-to-continuous neural network which consists of two main modules: Global Likelihood Estimation (GLE) and Continuous Position Estimation (CPE). In the GLE module, we construct an adaptive pairwise feature aggregator to fuse the acoustic features from microphone pairs, generating the global likelihood distribution of source over grids. Then, the CPE module derives continuous source position via a weighted sum of high-confidence grids. Compared with existing grid-based SSL methods, G2C-NET achieves better performance at equivalent grid resolution. Experimental results validate its effectiveness.

items.title: Fast Multichannel Nonnegative Matrix Factorization with Directivity Regularization for DOA-Informed Speech Separation
items.authors: Ryosuke Ono(Kyoto University; RIKEN); Aditya Arie Nugraha(RIKEN); Yoshiaki Bando(AIST; RIKEN); Kazuyoshi Yoshii(Kyoto University; RIKEN)
items.abstract: This paper addresses DOA-informed multichannel speech separation under overdetermined conditions, where the number of speakers does not exceed the number of microphones. We focus on FastMNMF, a BSS method robust to unknown acoustic environments. Since FastMNMF represents real-source spatial covariance matrices in a jointly diagonalized domain, its diagonal components correspond to virtual spatial components rather than the real sources themselves. We propose directivity-regularized FastMNMF, which encourages each pseudo-separation filter to pass signals from the target speaker direction and suppress those from other speaker directions while tolerating DOA errors. The separation matrix is updated using a closed-form VCD-based rule. Experiments with simulated noisy simultaneous speech mixtures show that the proposed regularization improves separation performance.

items.title: SpkGuideDOA: Speaker-wise Representation Guidance for Multiple Moving Speaker Localization
items.authors: Yongseok Choi(Hanyang University); Davin Kim(Hanyang University); Joon-Hyuk Chang(Hanyang University)
items.abstract: Localizing multiple moving speakers in dynamic acoustic environments requires resolving time-varying spatial cues under severe spatial-spectral overlap. To address this challenge, we propose SpkGuideDOA, a framework that enhances a spatial cue estimator with speaker-wise representation guidance while maintaining computational efficiency. An auxiliary guidance generator extracts implicit speaker representations from multi-channel magnitudes and injects them via residual modulation at a pooled resolution. Training is driven by a localization objective with an additional loss that stabilizes the guidance branch. Joint permutation-invariant training ensures consistent speaker assignment across modules. Experiments on simulated mixtures and the LOCATA dataset demonstrate improved localization performance while maintaining computational efficiency.

items.title: Quantifying the Uncertainty of Blindly Estimated Room Embeddings Using a Dispersion-Calibrated Score
items.authors: Yang Xiang(University of Surrey); Philipp Götz(International Audio Laboratories Erlangen); Emanuël A. P. Habets(International Audio Laboratories Erlangen); Andreas Walther(Fraunhofer Institute for Integrated Circuits IIS); Wenwu Wang(University of Surrey); Philip J. B. Jackson(University of Surrey)
items.abstract: Room embeddings derived from reverberant speech are often unreliable: speech content and recording degradation can alter the representation even when speaker, room, and source-receiver geometry remain unchanged, degrading downstream task performance. We propose a framework that learns room embeddings robust to speech-content variation and a representation-level uncertainty score from reverberant speech without downstream-task supervision. The embedding is anchored to a structured room impulse response (RIR) latent space and trained using a multi-view data structure with KullbackLeibler (KL)-based alignment; a multi-positive contrastive term further refines robustness. A lightweight uncertainty head is calibrated using the dispersion of corruption-induced embeddings and optimized with a rank-based objective. Across waveform- and spectrogram-level corruptions, the score is consistent with representation dispersion and enables effective selective prediction while requiring only a single utterance at inference.
